purpose: Four static intermediate pose drawings for user review, before any animation.

prompts.initial_comparison_board:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE LANDSCAPE FOUR-PANEL POSE COMPARISON BOARD, four sequential static in-between poses for a game character. NOT an animation.
Reference Image 1 is the APPROVED STANDING Elian and EXACT SCALE/PROPORTION/BUCKET MASTER. Image 2 is the APPROVED SQUAT reference for joint placement only. Match this boy's identity, face, hair, child proportions, outfit, silver eight-point star, cream sleeves, tan trousers, cuffed brown boots, dark brown outlines and ivory border. Same wooden full water bucket with TWO dark iron hoops, iron arch and wooden grip.

Critical task: draw four intermediate poses LEFT TO RIGHT on ONE SHARED SCALE. Treat the boy as the SAME puppet with identical head, torso, upper arm, forearm, thigh, shin, hand and boot dimensions in every panel. Treat the bucket as ONE RIGID COPIED OBJECT with IDENTICAL width, height, iron arch, wooden grip, perspective and horizontal water level in all four panels. Bucket width about 58% of head width, height including handle about 90% of hair-to-chin height. Do not shrink the bucket in squatting poses or shrink the boy in standing poses. No independent auto-framing per panel.
All four panels equal width, identical framing. Every pair of feet rests on exactly the same horizontal baseline near the bottom. Hip-width stable stance, both heels planted. Same foot locations relative to each panel across all four poses; bend knees over the toes. No stepping, sliding, tiptoe or kneeling.
Hair-to-chin HEAD SIZE MUST BE IDENTICAL across panels. Panel 1 head naturally lower on the canvas, panel 4 head highest; monotonic rising from 1 to 4. The crouched boy takes less HEIGHT, not a larger head. Thighs and shins unfold to raise the hips rather than getting longer or shorter. Preserve full figure and bucket, generous clear margins.

1: FIRST CLEARANCE, still a low squat with knees bent about 80 degrees, hips lowered, torso leaning 25 degrees, bucket just 3 cm off the floor in front between the boots. Right hand (viewer-left in the standing master) grips the wooden handle, left palm rests on its own thigh.
2: HALF RISE, knees extend to about 50 degrees, hips and shoulders clearly higher than 1, torso leaning 15 degrees. SAME size bucket rises about 10 cm above floor and moves only slightly to the carrying side. Same grip, free hand still lightly resting on thigh.
3: ALMOST UPRIGHT, knees only about 20 degrees flexed, hips now close to standing height, torso nearly vertical. Head must be clearly HIGHER than 2, NOT a shortened-body version of 2. SAME size bucket about 18 cm off floor, gently moving to the right-hand carrying side (viewer-left). Gripping arm mostly extended. Left hand has just released the thigh and hangs relaxed.
4: UPRIGHT CARRY SETTLE, standing at full height, knees relaxed, torso balanced. SAME size bucket at the carrying side, outside the leg silhouette, bottom about 20 cm off the ground. Same right-hand grip around wooden bar, straight connected wrist. Free left arm relaxed beside the opposite thigh.

Exactly one boy per panel, TWO arms and TWO opposite hands per boy, no duplicate limbs. The wooden bar passes inside the curled gripping fingers in ALL FOUR poses, not floating below the fist. No hand switches. Arms and legs visibly join the body.
Composition: wide landscape comparison sheet, four unobtrusive equal columns, shared warm off-white background and consistent tiny contact shadows. A small simple numeral '1', '2', '3', '4' above each respective pose, no other text. Large enough hands and knees to inspect. No props beyond the one bucket per pose, no scenery, no arrows, no blurred movement. The four pictures should function as consistent drawn key poses ready for visual review, not four independently resized illustrations.
prompts.bucket_size_refinement:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT TARGET: the supplied four-panel comparison board of Elian rising with a bucket.
Make a LOCAL CONSISTENCY CORRECTION, preserving the four poses, exact same head/face/hair/clothing artwork, background, column numbers and camera. Do not redesign Elian or create a new style.

1. RIGID BUCKET SIZE: use the bucket in panel 4 as the EXACT copied size/design/perspective template for ALL FOUR PANELS, including the iron arch and wooden handle. Panel 1's bucket is currently visibly too small: enlarge it approximately 10–12%. Panel 2's bucket needs approximately 4–5% enlargement. Panels 3/4 already have the intended size; preserve that size. All four buckets must end up with the same pixel height and width, same two iron hoops, same horizontal water surface and same wooden grip. This is one rigid object moving between frames. Do not change their size along with the boy's height.
Panel 1 is the first LIFT: lift that bucket and its connected gripping right hand enough to leave a small clearly visible gap (about 10–15 pixels at this board scale) between the bucket base and the common foot baseline. Adjust the gripping forearm/elbow naturally so the hand stays wrapped around the wooden bar; preserve arm segment lengths. Panel 2 has the same bucket a little higher, panel 3 higher again, panel 4 settled at the carrying height. Never let the base sink below the floor.

2. FIXED FEET: all four poses keep the SAME stable wider stance, with boot sole centres at approximately 25% and 78% across their respective equal-width columns. Match the planted floor level across all four panels. In panels 3 and 4 the legs should naturally straighten into that wider stance, not pull the feet inward. Preserve actual boot size and thigh/shin lengths, adjusting knee angles and hip height for the stance. Both soles grounded, no stepping, sliding or tiptoe. Preserve the rising sequence: panel 1 deep squat, 2 halfway up, 3 almost upright, 4 upright carrying. Keep identical head sizes; heads rise monotonically from 1 through 4. Exactly two anatomically opposite hands per figure with the SAME right gripping hand in every panel. Keep the free hand on thigh in 1/2 and relaxed at the side in 3/4.
Do not add anything else. Keep full-body framing, warm off-white background, brown outlines and ivory cut-paper border. No motion blur, no extra captions or animation.
prompts.planted_stance_refinement:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT TARGET: this four-panel Elian pose board. Make ONLY the following localized change to the LEGS BELOW THE BELT in PANELS 3 and 4. Keep panels 1 and 2 entirely unchanged. Keep every head, face, torso, arm, hand and ALL FOUR BUCKETS unchanged in size, position and design. The bucket-size correction is already approved; do not undo it.
The planted feet in 3 and 4 are still too close together. WIDEN the relaxed standing stance to the same foot spacing as panels 1 and 2, by moving each existing boot OUTWARD about 35–45 pixels at this image's scale. In each equal-width panel the two sole centres should be near 22% and 81% of that panel's width. Keep the boots exactly the same size and their sole contact on the existing common floor baseline. Do not add feet. Redraw the two trouser legs between the unchanged hips and the repositioned boots to connect naturally: knees follow toes, thighs and shins retain their lengths, no stretched trousers, no inward-collapsing knees. Panel 3 knees remain gently bent and panel 4 legs are comfortably straight in a stable wider carrying stance. Do not change the hip height or boy's total height in either panel.
This localized leg/foot repositioning makes the foot locations consistent through the four poses for later animation. Preserve the existing overall illustration exactly everywhere else: four numbers, four figures, head sizes, rising body heights, warm off-white background, brown contours, ivory border, bucket grip contacts and the now-equal bucket sizes. Static drawing only; no animation, no extra captions or objects.

limits: Illustrated comparison board, not pixel-registered sprite frames, a rig or Unity screenshots. No claim of exact pixel equality for independently drawn parts.
